export const meta = {
  name: 'parity-lever-hunt',
  description: 'Find concrete faithful optimizations for fa3_hopper.cu configs still below 0.95x vs FA3',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Hunt', detail: 'parallel deep-read FA3/cutlass vs our kernel per target cluster' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'dedupe + cross-rank candidates by EV, flag already-tried' },
  ],
}

const KERNEL = '/home/yak/fa3-cuda/kernels/fa3_hopper.cu'
const FA3 = '/home/yak/fa3-cuda/reference/vllm-flash-attention/hopper/'
const CUTLASS = '/home/yak/fa3-cuda/reference/cutlass'
const MEM = '/home/yak/.claude/projects/-home-yak-fa3-cuda/memory/fa3-perf-gap-closing.md'

const CAND_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    candidates: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          target: { type: 'string', description: 'config(s) this helps, e.g. attn_real_llama8b_pf_s16k' },
          lever: { type: 'string', description: 'concise name of the optimization' },
          mechanism: { type: 'string', description: 'WHY it helps: the specific inefficiency in our code vs what FA3 does, with file:line for both' },
          expected_impact_pp: { type: 'number', description: 'rough expected +pp gain, honest' },
          faithful: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true if it matches FA3/cutlass behavior (not benchmark-gaming)' },
          already_tried: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true if the memory notes this exact lever was tested' },
          risk: { type: 'string', description: 'correctness/regression risk + which other configs it touches' },
          concrete_change: { type: 'string', description: 'the specific code edit to make (function, lines, what to change)' },
        },
        required: ['target', 'lever', 'mechanism', 'expected_impact_pp', 'faithful', 'already_tried', 'concrete_change'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['candidates'],
}

const COMMON = `Our kernel: ${KERNEL} (a cutlass-free CUDA FA3 for Hopper sm90). FA3 reference: ${FA3}. Cutlass: ${CUTLASS}.
CRITICAL CONTEXT — read ${MEM} FIRST: it documents ~8 sessions of what's been TRIED and FAILED (do NOT re-propose those). The winning pattern just found: FA3's PagedKVManager broadcasts the computed int64 K/V row OFFSET across the 8 cooperating gather lanes instead of having each recompute ent*stride (8x redundant int64 muls) — this closed paged decode + qwen prefill. Look for MORE inefficiencies of that KIND: redundant per-lane/per-thread computation, a faithful FA3 schedule/layout we don't match, wasted instructions FA3 avoids.
Do NOT propose: benchmark-gaming (TMA on the arange page_table), de-scatter, parking/nanosleep waits, asymmetric K/V rings, STAGES=2 for paged, 240/24 registers for hd256, per-tile hd256 (all TRIED+FAILED per memory).
Report ONLY concrete, faithful, NOT-already-tried candidates with exact file:line for both our code and FA3's, the mechanism, and the specific edit. Be honest about expected_impact_pp (small is fine). Read-only; do not modify files.`

phase('Hunt')
const [pf, hd256, denselong, gather] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${COMMON}\n\nTARGET: attn_real_llama8b_pf_s2k (0.908x) and _s16k (0.925x) — paged bf16 hd128 causal PREFILL. It uses prefill_kernel (per-tile, NOT persist). Current ncu: tensor 67%, barrier 0.79 (FA3 74%/0.44). The COOP gather is already offset-broadcast-optimized. Deep-read FA3's hd128 paged prefill: mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp (consumer mma loop + ping-pong warp_scheduler_barrier), paged_kv.h, flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h. Compare to our prefill_kernel consumer mainloop (~lines 1310-1432) + COOP producer (~1216-1287). Find concrete levers to raise tensor 67->74 / cut barrier 0.79->0.44: redundant consumer work, softmax/wgmma interleave differences, ping-pong placement, producer issue-slot contention, any redundant int64/address math like the offset-broadcast. Rank by EV.`, { label: 'hunt:llama_pf', phase: 'Hunt', schema: CAND_SCHEMA }),

  () => agent(`${COMMON}\n\nTARGET: attn_dense_hd256_causal (0.878x) — DENSE bf16 hd256 causal PREFILL. It uses prefill_persist_kernel (persistent, TMA producer, NOT the COOP gather), CN=48/STAGES=3/CM=128. ncu: tensor 46%, acc_o[128] (128 fp32 regs/thread), 1 CTA/SM (occupancy-capped), barrier 2.01 (mostly harmless producer bar.sync). FA3 gets ~0.92 at CN=80/STAGES=2. Deep-read FA3's hd256 path: tile_size.h (kBlockN=80), mainloop_fwd_sm90 (RescaleOBeforeGemm, the 2-CTA cluster/TMA-multicast for non-causal, acc layout), flash_fwd_kernel_sm90.h. Compare to our prefill_persist_kernel (~lines 1450-1810) + hd256 dispatch (~line 2672) + launch (~2470-2504). Find concrete levers for the acc_o[128]/occupancy/46%-tensor problem that are NOT in the tried list (rescale-before/240regs/per-tile/CN80 all failed). Consider: FA3's exact acc tiling, any redundant compute in the big-head consumer, TMA producer efficiency, whether a different smem layout frees a stage. Rank by EV.`, { label: 'hunt:hd256', phase: 'Hunt', schema: CAND_SCHEMA }),

  () => agent(`${COMMON}\n\nTARGETS: dense bf16 hd128 LONG-CONTEXT still <0.96: attn_dense_hd128_nc4k (0.931), _large4k (0.923), _seq8k (0.941), _seq16k (0.953), _hd192_dv128 (0.937), _hd192_causal (0.968). These use prefill_persist_kernel (dense TMA persist, CM=128). Deep-read FA3's dense long-context mainloop (mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp consumer + tile scheduler tile_scheduler.hpp) vs our prefill_persist_kernel (~lines 1450-1810). Find concrete faithful levers: TMA multicast / cluster, tile-scheduler order (LPT / work distribution), softmax/wgmma overlap, any redundant compute. These share the persist kernel with hd256 so a lever may help both. Rank by EV and note cross-config impact.`, { label: 'hunt:dense_long', phase: 'Hunt', schema: CAND_SCHEMA }),

  () => agent(`${COMMON}\n\nTARGET: the COOP cp.async gather micro-architecture (prefill_kernel producer ~lines 1216-1287, shared by paged prefill + decode). It was just improved via offset-broadcast. Hunt for FURTHER faithful gather efficiencies vs FA3 paged_kv.h: (1) K and V share layout on the COOP path (HD==HDV) so koff==voff when strides match — can we broadcast ONE offset (2 shfl) instead of two (4 shfl)? Check k_row/v_row equality safety. (2) Is koffR/voffR (smem swizzle offset) recomputed redundantly? (3) cp.async granularity/coalescing vs FA3's kGmemElemsPerLoad. (4) Does FA3 issue K then V in separate commit groups or interleaved, and does our commit/publish (PF_PUBLISH) granularity thin the issue? (5) page-table LDG efficiency. For each, give the exact edit + safety guard + expected pp. Rank by EV.`, { label: 'hunt:gather', phase: 'Hunt', schema: CAND_SCHEMA }),
])

phase('Synthesize')
const all = [pf, hd256, denselong, gather].filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.candidates || [])
log(`collected ${all.length} raw candidates`)
const synth = await agent(`You are ranking candidate optimizations for a cutlass-free FA3 CUDA kernel to reach >=0.95x parity on the configs still below it. Here are ${all.length} raw candidates found by 4 analysis agents (JSON):\n\n${JSON.stringify(all, null, 2)}\n\nDedupe overlapping candidates. DROP any with already_tried=true or faithful=false. Cross-rank the survivors by expected value = expected_impact_pp × tractability × (breadth of configs helped) ÷ risk. Prefer the "redundant-computation / faithful-schedule-match" kind that just worked (offset-broadcast). Return the TOP candidates (up to 10) ranked best-first, each with target, lever, mechanism (with file:line), concrete_change, expected_impact_pp, risk. Be honest — if few are promising, return few.`, { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: CAND_SCHEMA })
return synth

candidates.target: attn_dense_hd128 large4k (0.923), seq8k (0.941), hd192_dv128 (0.937), hd192_causal, seq16k (0.953), hd256 — all causal persist configs (task #11, also touches #10)
candidates.lever: Causal persist work-ordering: global LPT (heaviest m-block across ALL heads handed out first, lightest last) instead of per-head LPT — match FA3's DynamicPersistentTileScheduler
candidates.mechanism: ncu MEASURED: large4k persist runs at only 58.1% SM vs seq16k 73.3% on the IDENTICAL mainloop with DRAM 7.8% -> pure makespan tail, not memory-bound. pf_work (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu ~918-924) maps work->tile per-(bi,hk): bi=work/(tiles_m*hkv), hk=rem/tiles_m, m_block=(tiles_m-1)-(rem-hk*tiles_m). Heavies are front-loaded WITHIN each head, but the LAST head's heavy m-block sits at global work index ~total-tiles_m, so the greedy work_ctr atomic hands it out near the global tail: one CTA runs a ~full-width heavy tile while ~131 CTAs drain the light tail and idle (overhang ~= heavy-tile time). FA3 orders GLOBALLY (reference/.../tile_scheduler.hpp:293-314 get_block_coord): head varies fastest, m_block next with block=num_m_blocks-1-block LPT, so the last tiles handed out are m_block=0 (lightest) across the section -> tail overhang ~= 1 n-block. These configs are compute-bound (2.6-7.8% DRAM), so an all-heads L2 section costs no DRAM penalty.
candidates.concrete_change: In pf_work (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu ~918) add an `int batch` param (pass at persist sites ~1560,1749 and fp8 ~2212,2279). Add a causal branch: `if(causal){ int nhb=hkv*batch; int m_local=work/nhb; int hbrem=work-m_local*nhb; bi=hbrem/hkv; hk=hbrem-bi*hkv; m_block=(tiles_m-1)-m_local; } else { keep current per-head mapping }`. Only the work->tile mapping changes; the dynamic greedy atomic and lock-step producer/consumer (both call pf_work) are untouched. Keep non-causal on the current per-head order (FA3 uses StaticPersistentTileScheduler there).
candidates.risk: Moderate. Boundary/index math must exactly cover the causal m_block ordering across all heads or results go wrong on ragged/varlen; only affects causal persist. Highest EV by far (6pp, ncu-measured makespan tail, 5-6 configs at once). Validate allclose + re-profile SM% on large4k.

candidates.target: attn_dense_hd256_causal (task #10, currently 0.878 — the config furthest from parity; dense bf16 hd256 persist, CN=48/STAGES=3/CM=128)
candidates.lever: PV as a single m64n256k16 RS wgmma instead of 2x m64n128k16 (extend the session-5 2xn64->n128 win to hd256)
candidates.mechanism: pv_boxes (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu:585-600) emits TWO pv_box128_body (m64n128, body at 556-574) for HDV==256 at lines 597-598 = 6 PV wgmma/tile at CN=48, where FA3's TiledMmaPV uses a SINGLE SM90_64x256x16_F32BF16BF16_RS per k-block (AtomLayoutPV N-atom=_1; reference/.../mainloop_fwd_sm90_tma_gmma_ws.hpp:100-113). hd256 is not LargeHeadDimV (>256) so RS n256 is permitted. The consumer here is compute-bound (tensor ~46%), so the 3 extra wgmma+fence/tile steal issue slots from softmax. The voffR<CN> layout (fa3_hopper.cu:176) lays the 4 dv-blocks at uniform byte stride BOX=CN*128, so ONE descriptor make_smem_desc(sV_base, LBO=CN*128, SW_V_SBO, 1) makes the m64n256 GMMA walk dv-blocks at 0,LBO,2LBO,3LBO = exactly our layout; the n128 form of this exact descriptor was already validated in session-5. Accumulator reg->(dv,row) mapping is unchanged (epilogue already reads a contiguous 256-wide C fragment).
candidates.concrete_change: In kernels/fa3_hopper.cu: (1) add PF_OUT128(a) macro (model on PF_OUT64O at ~445). (2) add pv_box256_body<T,O,N,CN> modeled on pv_box128_body (556-574) emitting wgmma.mma_async.m64n256k16.f32.bf16.bf16 with A={P[kb*4+0..3]} (RS, 4 regs), B=desc(dB=desc_add(baseV,v_doff(kb))), D=PF_OUT128 over CN/16 k-blocks. (3) in pv_boxes replace the two HDV>=128/HDV>=256 pv_box128_body calls, for HDV==256 only, with one pv_box256_body<T,0,HDV/2,CN>(...,make_smem_desc(sV_base,LBO,SW_V_SBO,1)); keep HDV==128/192/64 as-is.
candidates.risk: Low-medium. New wgmma shape + descriptor; a wrong descriptor NaNs immediately (correctness gate catches it, no silent regression). Touches only bf16 HDV==256. hd256 measurement is noisy (+/-3pp) so validate allclose first, then measure 2-3x. 2pp alone won't close 0.878->0.95 but it is the biggest single lever on the worst config; stack with C8.

candidates.target: ALL persist configs: nc4k (0.931), large4k (0.923), seq8k (0.941), seq16k (0.953), hd192_dv128, hd192_causal, hd256 (tasks #10, #11)
candidates.lever: Delete the redundant 2nd prologue fence.proxy.async in the persist consumer (make the persist prologue byte-identical to the per-tile kernel that already beats FA3)
candidates.mechanism: The persist consumer issues TWO fence.proxy.async.shared::cta per work-item: fa3_hopper.cu:1768 (after Q/barQf wait) and :1772 (after the first-K full[st0] wait, right before qk_gemm_g). The per-tile prefill_kernel — which memory records as BEATING FA3 (1.01-1.05x on dense causal hd128) — has only the post-Q fence and explicitly NONE between full[] and the first QK (comment at fa3_hopper.cu:1319: the cp.async/TMA complete-tx mbarrier already orders K/V writes before the wgmma reads on the same async proxy). FA3's dense consumer is likewise fence-free in steady state (mainloop_fwd_sm90:1214-1256). Line 1772 is thus redundant and sits on every work-item's critical path before the first QK; removing it frees consumer issue slots (matters most for many-work-item long-context and medium-uniform nc4k). Session-6 left this in ('not worth the correctness risk') but never tested it — the per-tile kernel proves it safe. This is the exact redundant-computation-removal KIND as the offset-broadcast win that just worked.
candidates.concrete_change: Delete line 1772 (asm volatile("fence.proxy.async.shared::cta;") in prefill_persist_kernel's consumer, after the full[st0] wait), keeping line 1768 (post-Q fence). This makes the persist prologue structurally identical to the proven per-tile prologue: Q-wait -> fence -> full-wait -> qk_gemm_g (no fence).
candidates.risk: Very low. Pure deletion; the per-tile kernel runs this exact fence-free ordering correctly today. Broadest + cheapest + safest survivor and the most on-pattern with the offset-broadcast win. Do it first alongside C7.

candidates.target: attn_real_llama8b_pf_s2k, attn_real_llama8b_pf_s16k, qwen3moe_pf (task #9: llama8b_pf 0.908/0.925; paged bf16 hd128 causal, per-tile prefill_kernel COOP)
candidates.lever: Signal empty[pst] immediately after wgmma_wait0(), before rescale_o_g + pack P (release the stage as early as FA3 does)
candidates.mechanism: In the per-tile prefill_kernel consumer (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu, the steady-state loop shown ~1385-1403): order is wgmma_wait0() -> rescale_o_g(acc_o,sc) (~64 FMUL) -> pack P (~CN/4 pack_2x) -> mbar_arrive(&empty[pst]). The empty signal that unblocks the producer's `while(!mbar_try_wait(&empty[st],ep))` (line 1257) is delayed ~100-130 issue-cycles past the point the stage is actually free. Stage pst is fully consumed at wgmma_wait0() (PV(li-1) read V[pst], QK(li-1) read K[pst] earlier); rescale_o_g and pack touch only registers (acc_o, P), never stage-pst smem. FA3 releases exactly here: mainloop_fwd_sm90:1272-1273 does warpgroup_wait<0>(); pipeline_v.consumer_release(...) BEFORE convert_type_out (pack) and rescale_o. Firing empty ~130 cycles sooner lets the COOP producer refill sooner and hot-spin less on empty[st], attacking the measured barrier 0.79->0.44 producer-lag residual; with ping-pong the lagging WG1 also arrives sooner.
candidates.concrete_change: In prefill_kernel's per-tile consumer, move `mbar_arrive(&empty[pst]);` from its current position (after the `for(i<CN/4) P[i]=pack_2x(...)` loop) to immediately after `wgmma_wait0();`, i.e. before `rescale_o_g(acc_o, sc);`. Leave the post-loop final empty arrive as-is. (persist consumer is disabled for paged, so no need to mirror there for these targets.)
candidates.risk: Very low. Pure reorder of one release-arrive relative to two register-only ops; stage pst is provably free at wait0. No new instructions; exactly matches FA3's release-before-pack ordering. Safe schedule-match, stacks cleanly with the already-landed idiv fix and offset-broadcast on the same paged loop.

candidates.target: attn_dense_hd256_fp8 / attn_kv_hd256_fp8_decode (native fp8 e4m3 hd256, prefill_fp8_kernel RS path; already ~0.91/1.02)
candidates.lever: fp8 PV as a single m64n256k32 RS wgmma instead of 2x m64n128k32 (fp8 analog of C5)
candidates.mechanism: pv_fp8_rs (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu:762+) loops NBOX=HDV/128=2 m64n128k32 boxes for HDV=256 (box b at vboff=box*128*128), so 2 PV wgmma where FA3's TiledMmaPV uses 1 wide n=headdim_v GMMA (mainloop_fwd_sm90:100-113). The transposed Vt tile is contiguous over the full HDV (VSTRIDE=HDV*128, fa3_hopper.cu:1860; the two 128-dv halves at byte 0 and 128*128), so a single m64n256k32 covers all 256 dv IF the SW8 dv-row stride is uniform across 256.
candidates.concrete_change: In pv_fp8_rs (762+), for HDV==256 emit ONE wgmma.mma_async.m64n256k32.f32.e4m3.e4m3 (RS, A={P16[kb*4..+3]}, B=make_smem_desc(sV_base+off,SW8_LBO,SW8_SBO,1), D=128 accumulators via a PF_OUT128 macro) over CN/32 k-blocks, replacing the NBOX=2 loop; keep HDV<=128 as-is. BEFORE trusting, bit-exact-check vs the current 2-box form: the fp8 Vt is K-major with a 128B fp8 swizzle (koff8R/SW8) and its uniform-stride-over-256 assumption is NOT independently validated the way the bf16 voffR case was.
candidates.risk: Medium. Descriptor uniform-stride over 256 dv is plausible (VSTRIDE contiguous) but unverified for the transposed K-major fp8 Vt — must bit-exact-check before use. fp8 hd256 is already near/at parity so upside is smaller and narrower than C5; do it only after C5 validates the same-kind change on bf16.

candidates.target: memory-bound paged decode (llama8b_dec_s16k, dec_b64_s4k, qwen3moe_dec_s32k — DRAM ~72% vs FA3 88%); NEUTRAL/low on the compute-bound dense targets
candidates.lever: Add L2 cache hints to TMA loads: EVICT_LAST for K/V, EVICT_FIRST for Q (FA3's exact policy)
candidates.mechanism: tma_box (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu:371-374) issues cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d WITHOUT the .L2::cache_hint qualifier (default EVICT_NORMAL). FA3 tags K/V loads EVICT_LAST (mainloop_fwd_sm90:791,805) so reused K/V tiles stay in L2 across m-blocks, and Q EVICT_FIRST (:858) since Q streams once. HONEST caveat: ncu shows the dense long-ctx targets are compute-bound (DRAM 2.6-7.8%, L2 29-38%) so this will NOT move large4k/seq16k/nc4k; the value is on the memory-bound paged decode where there is real DRAM headroom (72% vs FA3 88%). Genuine faithful FA3 mechanism we are missing.
candidates.concrete_change: Add a cache-hint tma_box variant emitting cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d...L2::cache_hint with a 5th u64 policy operand made once per kernel via createpolicy.fractional.L2::evict_last.b64 (and evict_first for Q). Use the K/V variant in load_kv (~1574-1585) and the evict_first policy in the tmaq/tmaq_gqa Q boxes (~1643,1653). Correctness-neutral (cache hints only).
candidates.risk: Near-zero (cache hints cannot change results). Impact honestly uncertain and likely nil on the dense targets; main hope is paged decode. Cheap to try given zero correctness risk, but do not expect it to close a dense config.

candidates.target: attn_kv_hd256_fp8_decode + fp8 paged prefill (prefill_fp8_kernel COOP resolve) — RESIDUAL scope of the idiv fix that was NOT extended to the fp8 path
candidates.lever: Extend the already-landed pow2 shift/mask (bshift/bmask) from the bf16 COOP producer to the fp8 COOP page-table resolve (kill runtime idiv/imod there too)
candidates.mechanism: The bf16 paged COOP producer at fa3_hopper.cu:1265-1266 ALREADY uses `key >> bshift` / `key & bmask` / `blk << bshift` (uncommitted working tree — this is candidates 1 & 11 already done for the bf16 targets). But the fp8 COOP resolve still emits raw software idiv/imod: fa3_hopper.cu:2001-2002 (`page_table[... + key/block_size]`, `blk*block_size + key%block_size`) and 2027-2028. Same issue-slot cost, same proven fix (FA3 uses cutlass::FastDivmod, paged_kv.h:145). Also line 1314-1315 (CONV producer) and 1610-1611 (persist COOP, dead for paged) still divide but are off the fp8 target's hot path.
candidates.concrete_change: Compute bshift/bmask once (warp-uniform, as done at 1254-1255) in prefill_fp8_kernel's COOP producer, then replace `key/block_size`->`key>>bshift`, `key%block_size`->`key&bmask`, `blk*block_size`->`blk<<bshift` at 2001-2002 and 2027-2028. Guard with the existing pow2 assumption (all vLLM/bench block_size are pow2). Optionally also 1314-1315 for consistency.
candidates.risk: Very low (same guarded pow2 transform already validated on the bf16 path; isolated to fp8 COOP). Small EV and narrow (fp8 paged only) because the headline bf16 paged win is already in the tree — this is just the un-extended tail of that same change.

candidates.target: all paged COOP prefill configs (llama8b_pf, qwen3moe_pf) — task #9
candidates.lever: Carry a rotating ring index (0->1->2->0) + toggled phase (FA3 PipelineState) instead of recomputing li%STAGES / (li-1)%STAGES / (li/STAGES)&1 every iteration
candidates.mechanism: STAGES=3 (not pow2), so st=li%STAGES, pst=(li-1)%STAGES, fp=(li/STAGES)&1 (consumer) and st=li%STAGES, ep=((li/STAGES)-1)&1 (producer, line 1257) each compile to magic-number mod/div-by-3 sequences (~4-5 SASS ops each) of pure index arithmetic on both hot loops. FA3 carries a PipelineState that increments/wraps and toggles phase on wrap (mainloop_fwd_sm90:1246-1247; pipeline.hpp). Replacing our modulo with `pst=st; if(++st==STAGES){st=0; fp^=1;}` removes that per-iteration integer math from the compute-bound consumer and issue-bound producer.
candidates.concrete_change: In prefill_kernel consumer, replace per-iteration st/pst/fp with a loop-carried st (init to the pre-loop tile's stage, advance pst=st; if(++st==STAGES)st=0;) and a phase bit toggled on wrap. Do the same in the producer (carry st and the empty-phase ep). Keep post-loop indices computed once.
candidates.risk: Low-moderate. Must reproduce the EXACT st/pst/fp/ep sequence — an off-by-one on phase deadlocks or reads a stale stage. Uncertain gain: ptxas may already strength-reduce li%3 to a rotating counter (then ~0pp), though less cleanly when both li%3 and li/3 are live (our case). Do after C2; verify SASS actually loses the mod-by-3.

candidates.target: attn_real_llama8b_pf_s16k only (long-context causal, ~127 interior unmasked tiles)
candidates.lever: Statically split the consumer into a masked boundary loop + a mask-free interior loop (FA3's two-loop structure), dropping the per-interior-tile pf_mask fast-out branch
candidates.mechanism: Every steady-state iteration calls pf_mask (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu, def ~266-283) which even on fully-visible interior tiles computes kmax and evaluates `if(kmax<seqlen_k && (!causal||kmax<=qlo)) return;` (~5 ALU ops + branch) on the wgmma_wait1->softmax critical window. For causal s16k only the last diagonal tile is masked, so ~127 iterations pay the branch for nothing. FA3 removes it structurally (mainloop_fwd_sm90:1283-1323): a causal-masking loop down to n_block_min_causal_local_mask, then a separate no_mask interior loop with zero mask instructions.
candidates.concrete_change: Split the consumer `for(li=1; li<n_cnt; ++li)` loop: run interior tiles without pf_mask, then a short tail loop (last 1-2 tiles) that calls pf_mask, computing the boundary-tile count once. Guard the EXTRA (softcap/SWA) path to keep pf_mask_win on all tiles.
candidates.risk: Moderate (hot-loop refactor; boundary count must exactly cover the causal diagonal AND the seqlen_k partial tile or ragged/varlen goes wrong). Smallest EV of the paged levers; only worth it after C2 and only if s16k is still <0.95.

candidates.lever: 2-CTA cluster + TMA multicast for the non-causal dense path (FA3's Enable_cluster) — LISTED LAST, likely not worth it
candidates.mechanism: FA3 launches ClusterShape<2,1,1> with SM90_TMA_LOAD_MULTICAST for K/V exactly when bf16 && hd>=128 && !causal && !local && !split && !paged && !varlen && ceil(seqlen_q/kBlockM)%2==0 (flash_fwd_launch_template.h:222-228); mcast_mask_kv (mainloop:779-786) fills both CTAs' smem with one TMA load, halving L2->smem K/V traffic. nc4k is the only target this applies to (all others are causal). candidates.concrete_change: Add a non-causal persist launch variant with dim3 cluster(2,1,1) via cudaLaunchKernelEx + cluster-scoped full[] mbarriers + a multicast tma_box (cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d...multicast::cluster with a ctamask), gated like FA3 (bf16 && HD>=128 && !causal && !paged && rep==1 && tiles_m%2==0).
candidates.risk: High + large. Cluster launch, cluster-scoped mbarriers, mcast mask, __cluster_dims__, and cluster-aware continuous-ring staging = hang-prone. Given nc4k is compute-bound, expected gain is small and off the critical path. Do NOT pursue unless nc4k is still <0.95 after C7 + C8 (which directly attack its makespan/issue-slot bottlenecks).
